title: Escalation: when to pass it on and with what information

videos.script: Some tickets are not yours to solve. The fault is in a system you have no access to, or in a program another team owns, or it needs a decision above yours. {{notyours}} Escalating is not giving up, and it is not throwing the ticket over a wall. It is handing it to the person who can solve it, with everything they need to start where you stopped. {{handing}} In this lesson a sales system stops answering. You find the cause, you decide not to fix it yourself, and you pass it on with the evidence packed. {{sales}} Then you keep the ticket's promise to the user, because escalating moves the work, not the responsibility. {{promise}}
